neighbours.label: ' take' / ' taken' in 'take over' = seize control or overrun (not other senses of take)
fire: If you don't prune the mint, it will take over the whole flower bed.
The generals plotted to take over the government before the election.
Blackberry bushes have taken over the back of the yard.
Try not to let work take over your weekends.
Invasive carp could take over the lake within a decade.
The army had taken over the radio station by midnight.
Don't let fear take over when you step on stage.
Algae will take over the pond if the water gets too warm.
quiet: If you don't prune the mint, it will grow very tall by August.
The generals plotted to overthrow the government before the election.
We take the bus to school every morning.
Try to take a short break every afternoon.
It can take a decade for the lake to recover.
The army had captured the radio station by midnight.
She had taken the photographs at midnight.
Please take your shoes off at the door.

notes: Card: ' take' x8, ' taken' x5 of the top 32, nearly all 'take over' (plants, OCD, empires), plus ' aggressively' turning a lawn and aliens TAKING people. Probes: take over 0.32-0.82 (weeds highest); 'take a shower', 'take about three hours', 'taken piano lessons' 0.00-0.03; 'seize the capital', 'overrun' 0.15-0.18, so the meaning without the word leaks a little.
